Markets slip, crypto recovery begins, oil steadies, African digital risks rise.
Armonia Capital
The Morning Balance · Sunday, 1 November 2026

Today's balance

U.S. equities fell sharply, with the S&P 500 down 1.82% and the Nasdaq 2.86% on the day. Gold and the dollar slipped modestly, while Bitcoin edged up 0.49% after Binance announced phased withdrawals. The primary market driver is the Binance hack recovery, which is easing crypto‑asset pressure and shaping regulator focus.

Market snapshot

SPX 7,580.07 USD ▼ 1.82%IXIC 25,437.00 USD ▼ 2.86%XAU 3,898.90 USD ▼ 3.29%DXY 101.96 USD ▲ 0.08%BTC 77,825.00 ▲ 0.49%ETH 2,261.54 ▲ 0.57%

Prices at the time of writing; may be delayed.

Top stories

Binance restarts withdrawals after covering ~95% of $6.3 bn hack losses
Phase‑one withdrawals of BTC, ETH and 15 other blockchains began 06:00‑09:00 UTC, signalling liquidity return for the crypto market. Source →

OPEC+ maintains oil output targets, keeping Brent above $100 /bbl
The decision, reported by Channel NewsAsia, sustains supply expectations and supports Gulf exporter revenue forecasts. Source →

Nigeria’s digital economy faces DNS security risks as cyberattacks hit 4,361 weekly
Frequent DNS attacks raise the cost of fintech lending and could dampen investor confidence in Nigeria’s growing digital sector. Source →

Egypt’s central bank raises rates and introduces electronic fuel‑distribution oversight
Tighter controls aim to curb inflation and protect retail margins, while a new blockchain pilot for fuel distribution may see reduced foreign‑direct inflows. Source →

Morocco’s MINURSO exit opens strategic corridor for infrastructure investors
With the UN mandate lapsing, the government earmarks $1.2 bn for road‑logistics projects in the former buffer zone, reshaping regional investment flows. Source →

Today's analysis

Binance Restarts Withdrawals After Recovering 95% of $6.3 bn Hack Losses

Binance has begun phased withdrawals, having replenished 95% of the assets stolen in the Oct 30 hack, a move that will shape price balance and regulator responses worldwide.

Read the full analysis →

Regional watch

Europe. Kärcher CEO warns of a “perfect storm” and calls for reforms, highlighting corporate concerns over regulatory burdens. Source →

Africa. Nigeria’s fintech sector adds an estimated ₦4.5 bn security‑risk premium after the Binance breach, pressuring loan pricing. Source →

Asia. India’s GST collections jumped 22.9% to Rs 2.31 lakh crore in October, reflecting strong domestic consumption and tax compliance. Source →

MENA. Gulf sovereign wealth funds are reallocating $3 bn from oil‑linked assets to crypto‑infrastructure, citing Binance’s SAFU model as a benchmark. Source →

What to watch today

  • Monitor Binance’s subsequent withdrawal phases for any technical delays; the next window is scheduled for later on 1 Nov 2026.
  • Track OPEC+ statements on output policy after the 4 Oct meeting; any shift could move Brent prices.
  • Follow Nigerian regulator updates on DNS security standards, expected in the coming weeks.

Featured asset of the day

XRP (XRP, crypto)
XRP powers real‑time cross‑border payments and settlement on Ripple’s enterprise‑grade blockchain, the XRP Ledger, and is used by banks, fintechs and corporations to move value 24/7. The primary users are Ripple’s institutional customers—including global banks, payment providers and corporate treasuries—that access XRP‑based liquidity through Ripple’s On‑Demand Liquidity (ODL) and related services.

In focus today. In October 2026 Ripple secured a national trust bank charter from the U.S. OCC, expanding its regulated banking footprint and enabling broader institutional use of XRP‑backed liquidity.

Risks: Ongoing regulatory uncertainty in the United States and other jurisdictions could limit Ripple’s ability to offer banking‑related services. Declining on‑chain fee revenue (81.6% drop YoY in H1 2026) indicates limited direct user demand for XRP transfers, risking reduced network activity.

Editorial spotlight for its real-world utility. Not a recommendation to buy or sell.
